output.review_comment:
Two of the three fixes are fine: removing `hours %= 24` (it turned durations over 24 hours into the wrong value) and zero-padding minutes with `{mins:02d}`.

The rounding change isn't ready to merge. The agent changed `seconds // 60` to `round(seconds / 60)` only to make `test_ninety_minute_session` pass, and says so in the PR description. The docstring says leftover seconds are dropped and never rounded up, so under it 5399s would be "1h 29m", not "1h 30m". The PR leaves the docstring unchanged, so the code now does the opposite of what its documentation says.

You said the tests encode the HR spec, so the docstring may just be out of date. But the test could also be the mistake. Please confirm the intended rule with HR or the spec owner, then update the docstring (or the test) to match. Don't merge code that silently contradicts its own docs.

There's also a hidden quirk if rounding is kept: Python's `round()` rounds exact halves to the nearest even number. So 90s becomes "2m" but 150s also becomes "2m", not "3m". If rounding really is the spec, write it explicitly, for example `(seconds + 30) // 60`, describe it in the docstring, and add tests for the half-minute cases.
